title: SYSK Selects: How The Moonwalk Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun (originally aired July 1, 2016) of the episode on the moonwalk. Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant open with banter about moonwalking, books and Stephen King, then trace the dance's history from Cab Calloway's the Buzz and Sammy Davis Jr.'s collegiate/camel walk, through Bill Bailey's 1955 Apollo moonwalk, Marcel Marceau's air walk, and mime's 1970s popularity, to Jeffrey Daniel's backslide on Solid Gold and Michael Jackson's 1983 Motown special performance of Billie Jean. They discuss who taught Jackson the move, the popping, locking and breakdancing lineage (Electric Boogaloos, the Lockers, Rerun), and give a step-by-step explanation of how to do the moonwalk (backslide). The episode also includes a correction about the Gettysburg Address episode (casualties vs. dead, and army percentages) and a listener mail about bias and funding in scientific research.

segments.title: Opening banter: moonwalking, books and Stephen King
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke about who can moonwalk, trade reading habits (Josh's fiction, Chuck's nonfiction and Civil War books), discuss Sapiens, Dean Koontz and Stephen King, and set up the topic.

segments.title: Early history: Cab Calloway, Sammy Davis Jr. and the camel walk
segments.summary: The hosts say the moonwalk goes back to the 1930s, citing Cab Calloway's the Buzz and the collegiate or camel walk, which Sammy Davis Jr. performed, with James Brown daring him to do it.

segments.title: Bill Bailey's 1955 Apollo moonwalk and the air walk
segments.summary: Bill Bailey is described as doing a legitimate moonwalk off the stage at the Apollo in 1955. The hosts note the move seemed to die with him. Marcel Marceau's air walk is compared and distinguished from the moonwalk.

segments.title: Mimes in the 1970s and why people dislike mimes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the 1970s popularity of mimes, including Shields and Yarnell's TV show, and speculate on why people dislike mimes.

segments.title: Jeffrey Daniel, the backslide, Shalamar and Michael Jackson's Motown performance
segments.summary: Jeffrey Daniel of Shalamar performed the backslide on Soul Train and Solid Gold, inspired partly by Shields and Yarnell. Michael Jackson performed the moonwalk during Billie Jean on the NBC Motown special. Accounts of who taught Jackson the move are discussed, along with his choreographers.
topics: who taught Michael Jackson the moonwalk

segments.title: Popping, locking and breakdancing lineage
segments.summary: The hosts trace popping and locking to the Electric Boogaloos and the Lockers, with Don Campbell as locking's originator and Rerun from What's Happening as an example. They reflect on hip hop and breakdancing as new art forms.

segments.title: How to moonwalk step by step and the lean
segments.summary: Josh gives a step-by-step description of the moonwalk (backslide): flat foot dragged back while the other heel lifts, with long stride and snapped feet. The hosts mention the lean tutorial by Robert Hoffman.
